title: Accounts Payable Administrator
description:
My client is seeking an organised and detail-oriented Accounts Payable Administrator to join their finance team in Birkenhead.The role will focus on processing supplier invoices and payments, assisting with credit card reconciliations and providing general administrative support, including vehicle administration.
Key Responsibilities
Accounts Payable and Finance
- Process incoming supplier invoices, checking details against purchase orders and ensuring the correct references and cost codes are recorded.
- Obtain the necessary authorisations and process approved invoices through the relevant finance systems.
- Prepare and process weekly supplier payment runs.
- Respond to supplier queries professionally and promptly.
- Assist with credit card transaction processing and reconciliations.
- Provide general finance and administrative support as required.
- General Administration and Operational Support
- Answer incoming telephone calls and direct enquiries appropriately.
- Liaise with drivers and vehicle maintenance providers to arrange servicing and maintenance.
- Update vehicle insurance details when vehicles are exchanged.
- Check and process driver mileage claims.
- Maintain accurate records and up-to-date documentation.

Skills and Experience
The successful candidate will have:
- GCSEs or equivalent, including English and Maths at grade C/4 or above.
- At least three years' experience in an accounts payable role.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Experience using finance systems and processing supplier invoices.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- A professional and helpful approach when dealing with colleagues, suppliers and external contacts.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team.

This role offers a basic salary of up to 29,000 depending on experience, 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, company pension, death in service

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller

Salary: Circa £28,000 FTE

Permanent Full-time or potentially part-time

Experienced in Credit Control? Looking for a fresh opportunity?

Hoot Recruit is recruiting on behalf of an established business looking for a Credit Controller to join its finance team.

We're looking for someone who knows their way around credit control, enjoys dealing with customers and is confident chasing payments while maintaining good working relationships.

You'll be joining an experienced team, working alongside an existing Credit Controller who will be on hand to provide guidance and support as they move into another position within the business.

What you'll be doing
- Managing outstanding customer payments
- Contacting customers by phone and email to chase overdue invoices
- Maintaining accurate records of payments and outstanding balances
- Resolving invoice and payment queries
- Building positive relationships with customers
- Reconciling customer accounts
- Working closely with the wider finance team to keep debtor balances under control

What we're looking for
- Previous credit control experience is essential
- Confident and professional telephone manner
- Comfortable having conversations about overdue payments
- Good organisational skills and attention to detail
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Friendly, approachable and proactive attitude

What's on offer?
- Salary circa £28,000 (pro rata for part-time)
- Permanent opportunity
- Potential flexibility around working hours
- Part-time hours may be considered, ideally spread across five days
- Support from an experienced finance team
- Stable, established business

This could be a great opportunity for an experienced Credit Controller who wants a role where they can make a real contribution without necessarily having to manage a team.

title: Customer Service Advisor - Property Management
description:
Job Description

We are looking for an enthusiastic and highly motivated Customer Service Advisor (Also known locally as a Property Manager) to complement our Property Management Team within our Lettings Department in Birkenhead: The Wirral. As a Customer Service Advisor, you will provide property management and tenancy support services to branches, landlords and tenants.

Starting Salary £25,000

What's in it for you as a Customer Service Advisor?
- Get full training and development
- A good understanding of the residential lettings industry
- Fast paced, fun environment
- Regular team meetings
- Full company briefings
- A career pathway

Key responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor.
- Act as a central point of contact managing the effective resolution of queries from clients and colleagues
- Coordinating urgent and routine repairs and maintenance
- Liaising with trades people/contractors and keeping customers up to date
- Organising safety inspections and managing remedial works
- Liaising with landlords following regular property visits
- Assisting customers with general tenancy queries
- Carrying out weekly partnership calls with colleagues and welcome calls with new customers
- Dealing promptly and courteously to communication with landlord, tenants, contractors, and internal partners
- Providing a first-class service to maximise customer retention
- Ensuring personal and team deadlines are met, service levels maintained and KPI's achieved

Skills and Experience required to be successful as a Customer Service Advisor.
- Strong customer service skills and confident communicator
- Good team player
- Customer focussed Contact or Call centre experience preferred
- Ability to stay calm under pressure
- Excellent negotiation and influencing skills
- Excellent planning and organisational skills
- Good analytical ability

Benefits
- Opportunity to undertake industry qualifications, with a £1,000 salary increase on passing
- Aviva Digi care + workplace / Car leasing and cycle to work scheme
- Colleague discount scheme / Perks at work / Gym discounts
- Life assurance / Workplace pension scheme
- 23 days annual leave, increasing with length of service (and your birthday off)

Connells Group UK is an equal opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of , race, disability, age, sexual orientation, transgender status, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

title: Corporate Property Coordinator
description:
Job Description

We're looking for a passionate CorporateProperty Coordinator to complement our established team based within our Corporate Lettings Centre in Birkenhead the Wirral, Merseyside. As our Property Coordinator, you will provide property management and tenancy administration support services to branches, landlords and tenants.

Benefits of a Corporate Property Coordinator:
- Salary: £25,000
- Support in training towards ARLA - NFOPPqualifications
- Industry-leading training and development
- Demonstrable career ladder
- Opportunities for progression
- Collaborative, rewarding, and fun environment
- Team incentives
- Understanding of operations within an estate agency business

Key responsibilities of a Corporate Property Coordinator

The main purpose of your role is to provide a property management and tenancy administrationsupport service to branches, landlords, and tenants. You will also coordinate and prepare the renewal of tenancies and liaise with contractors to ensure repair/maintenance works are carried out in time and to agreed standards.

Skills and experience required to be a successful Corporate Property Coordinator
- Outstanding Customer Service skills
- Solid administration skills
- Resilient, positive, numerate and detail-oriented
- Organised and able to prioritise workload in a faced paced environment
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- IT literate (MS Office, internet, email systems)
- Experience in areas such as the administration of ground rent demands, buildings insurance arrangements and renewals, Section 20 consultations, and LPE1 enquiries would be highly advantageous. A sound understanding of block management, including leasehold legislation and the day-to-day management of residential developments, would also be desirable. Candidates with this additional experience will be well placed to support the wider Property Management function and contribute to the continued growth of the department.

Connells Group UK is an equal opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of , race, disability, age, sexual orientation, transgender status, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of colour are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Connells Group we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. So, if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't fit perfectly with every aspect of the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other opportunities.

title: Legal Secretary / Legal Assistant
description:
Your new company
Are you an experienced Legal Secretary or Legal Assistant looking to join a friendly, established law firm where you can become a valued member of the team?We are recruiting on behalf of a well-regarded law firm based on the Wirral for an experienced Legal Secretary / Legal Assistant to provide high-quality administrative and secretarial support across a varied caseload.This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous experience within a legal environment who enjoys a busy, varied role and takes pride in providing a professional and organised support service.You will work across areas including Family Law, Probate and Personal Injury, making this particularly suited to someone who enjoys variety rather than supporting one specific area of law.
Your new role
The position is offered full time. Monday to Friday and fully based on site. You will be joining a small and supportive team who offer career opportunities.
Some of your duties will include but not limited to
Providing day-to-day secretarial and administrative support to fee earners
Preparing, formatting and amending legal documents and correspondence
Audio and copy typing
Managing diaries, appointments and meetings
Handling incoming telephone calls and dealing professionally with client enquiries
Opening, maintaining and closing client files
Liaising with clients, courts and other third parties
Preparing documentation and correspondence relating to Family Law, Probate and Personal Injury matters
Maintaining accurate electronic and paper-based records
Supporting fee earners with the smooth progression of cases
Ensuring confidential and sensitive information is handled appropriately
Providing general administrative support across the wider office when required
What you'll need to succeed
You will need to come from a legal secretary / legal assistant background and possess the following in order to be considered for the role.
Previous experience as a Legal Secretary, Legal Assistant or Legal Administrator
Experience working within a law firm or legal environment
Strong typing and document production skills
Excellent attention to detail and organisational ability
Confident written and verbal communication skills
The ability to prioritise a varied workload and work to deadlines
A professional and approachable manner when dealing with clients
Good IT skills and experience using Microsoft Office and legal case management systems
Experience in Family Law, Probate and/or Personal Injury would be particularly advantageous.
What you'll get in return
Friendly and supportive environment
Free parking
Progression opportunities
What you need to do now
If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: School Administrator
description:
Job Title: School Administrator
Location: Wirral
Start Date: Immediate
Contract Type: Full-Time, Term Time Only

Are you organised, professional, and confident working in a busy school environment? Do you have strong administrative and communication skills and enjoy working with staff, students, parents, and visitors? We're looking for a reliable and experienced School Administrator to support a school in Wirral, with an immediate opportunity available.

About the Role:

We are seeking a School Administrator to provide efficient administrative and front-of-house support within a busy school office. You'll be responsible for assisting with the day-to-day running of the school office, maintaining accurate records, responding to enquiries, and supporting staff, pupils, parents, and visitors.

Key Responsibilities:

Provide general administrative and reception support to the school
Answer telephone calls, respond to emails, and deal with enquiries professionally
Welcome and assist parents, visitors, staff, and pupils
Maintain accurate records and update school databases and systems
Support with attendance and pupil administration
Prepare documents, letters, reports, and other school correspondence
Assist with filing, photocopying, data entry, and general office duties
Handle confidential information appropriately and follow safeguarding procedures
Work collaboratively with teaching and support staff to ensure the smooth running of the school office

What We're Looking For:

Previous administrative or reception experience
Excellent organisation and attention to detail
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Confident using Microsoft Office and computer-based systems
Ability to manage competing priorities in a busy environment
A professional, friendly, and approachable manner
Understanding of confidentiality and safeguarding requirements
A valid enhanced DBS (or willingness to apply for one)

Previous experience working within a school or education setting
Experience using school management systems such as SIMS, Arbor, Bromcom, or similar
Experience with attendance, admissions, safeguarding, or pupil administration

title: Project Assistant
description:
Job Title: Project Assistant
Contract Type: Permanent
Salary: £26,227.50 per annum
Working Hours: 37.5 Hours per week
Working Pattern: Shift work - including weekends
Location: Rose Brae, Wirral

If you share our values and are excited about making a significant impact at Riverside, please ensure you attach a current CV and covering letter. At Riverside we recruit to potential not just on skills and experience, so we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the essential criteria on the job description.
Please note that whilst we will accept applications on the basis of any form of valid legal permission to work in the UK, we will be surrendering the Riverside Sponsorship licence, so for the avoidance of doubt, we are unable to apply for any further sponsorships whether on behalf of existing colleagues or candidates.

The difference you will make as a Project Assistant
You will be key in the day-to-day running of one of our supported housing services. We don't run care homes, so there's no need to provide personal care. The priority in your role includes the safety and wellbeing of everyone in our accommodation, including our customers.
Working with people who have a range of needs, you could be doing any number of things. From supporting customers in conversations with calls from their GP, Social Services, or Benefits teams - to dealing with the emergency services including the Police and Ambulance, when the need arises.
You'll log all incidents to make sure we have an accurate record of events. And when a customer leaves, you will clean and prepare their room, ready for the next occupant.

About you
We are looking for someone with:
- Experience of working with people in a customer facing environment
- An understanding of supporting vulnerable people - this could include having your own lived experience of homelessness or drug or alcohol addiction

Why Riverside?
At Riverside, we're a housing association with a difference - enhancing the everyday for all our customers. For 90 years, we've been revitalising neighbourhoods and supporting communities by providing the homes they need to live full, fulfilling and rewarding lives.
We have a portfolio of over 75,000 affordable residential and retirement homes across the UK. Our work ranges from homelessness services to social care, employment support to retirement living, and we need the best people on board to help us.
Working with us, you'll enjoy:
- Competitive pay & generous pension
- 25 days holidays plus bank holidays
- Flexible working options available
- Investment in your learning, personal development and technology
- A wide range of benefits

Diversity and Inclusion at Riverside:
We are inclusive. At Riverside, we value diversity in all its forms. We foster a workplace where all individuals are respected, empowered, and heard. Our commitment to inclusivity drives our success and enriches the lives of our customers and colleagues.
Riverside is a Disability Confident Employer and operates a Guaranteed Interview Scheme for any applicant who declares they have a disability. If the applicant meets the minimum requirements for the role (as set out in the role profile and/or person specification) they will be guaranteed an interview.

Applications may close before the deadline, so please apply early to be considered

Role Profile
We use Psychologically Informed approaches and Trauma Informed Care principles to support our customers to make positive choices, develop new ways of thinking and take steps towards independence, by:
- Assisting in the planning and delivery of a range of personalised support and move-on plans
- Understanding the risk management process and assisting the team to organise and undertake regular reviews of support and risk
- Inspiring and motivating customers to meet agreed outcomes and develop life skills
- Assisting customers with day-to-day support and tenancy-related matters
- Assisting the team to identify and promote opportunities for employment, education and training and support customers to access them
- Signposting customers to appropriate external support services, such as food banks and other community resources
- Supporting customers to be 'tenancy ready', enabling successful move on
- Supporting customers to be financially independent through budgeting plans and maximising income
- Supporting and monitoring customers' healthcare needs, ensuring appropriate contact with healthcare professionals
- Empowering customers to move towards self-management of their medication by following Riverside's medication procedure
- Maintaining and updating clear, accurate and strengths-based records on the appropriate digital platform
- Assisting in the promotion of customer involvement and consultation
- Assisting with the delivery of a range of group work sessions

Deliver a support service:
- Support the delivery of the referral process for new customers
- Contribute to the delivery of a housing management service, including income collection and providing customers with tenancy-related support
- Work with customers to maintain a safe environment, including reporting any repairs or health and safety concerns
- Clean and prepare customer rooms as appropriate
- Resolve difficult and challenging situations in a sensitive and informed way, balancing the needs of the individual with the safety of the service
- Ensure customer safety by following local safeguarding procedures, recognizing and acting on any risks and escalating appropriately
- Contribute to and maintain local partnerships to ensure availability of a holistic range of support for customers
- Carry out day-to-day administration and operational duties
- Maintaining and updating financial administration systems

title: Document Controller / Project Administrator
description:
Document Controller / Project Administrator

Prenton Hybrid Permanent/ Fixed Term ASAP Start

Walker Sime is looking for a Document Controller / Project Administrator to join our team in Prenton, supporting the delivery of a major infrastructure programme.

This is a broader role combining document control, project administration and coordination, including supporting the administration of NEC contracts.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working in a structured project environment, is comfortable managing detailed information and documentation, and can work confidently with different stakeholders.

About Walker Sime

Walker Sime is a UK-based construction consultancy providing project management, quantity surveying and commercial management services across a range of sectors.

As part of HanmiGlobal, we combine the feel and relationships of a UK consultancy with the scale, expertise and opportunities of a global project management business.

The Role

You'll provide document control and administrative support to the project team while also helping coordinate customer applications and associated works.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining controlled project documentation
- Supporting the administration of NEC contracts and associated records
- Maintaining document registers, trackers and project information
- Uploading, reviewing, distributing and filing documentation through the appropriate systems
- Supporting the coordination and progression of customer applications
- Liaising with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders
- Monitoring actions and following up on outstanding information
- Ensuring documentation remains accurate, current and appropriately controlled
- Providing wider project administration and coordination support to the team

Ideally, you'll bring:
- Previous document control or project administration experience
- Experience working within a project or programme environment
- Strong document management and administration skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Strong organisation and coordination skills
- Confidence working with multiple stakeholders
- Experience supporting NEC4 contracts would be advantageous
- Previous experience with Autodesk document management systems would be beneficial
- Experience within infrastructure, utilities or construction would be useful, but isn't essential

Working Pattern

This is a hybrid role, with 2 days per week based in our Prenton office and 3 days working from home. For your first two weeks, you'll be based in Prenton full-time while completing your training.

We're looking for someone who can start as soon as possible.

Apply now or get in touch.

Please note, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK.

title: Sales Administrator
description:
ROLE: Sales Administrator
HOURS: 37.5 Monday - Friday 08:00 - 16:00 - 6mth FTC
SALARY: £12.93 p/hr plus excellent benefits
BENEFITS: Healthcare Cash Plan, 3x Salary Life Assurance, High Street Discounts, Staff Discount
BASE: Site Based - Vista Panels, Prenton
Eurocell are a stock market listed Plc and the market leader for uPVC products within the building industry. We know that our people are our greatest asset, we are successful, dynamic, ambitious and looking for great team players to grow with us.
We are delighted to be recruiting for an experienced Sales Administrator to support the Sales office and wider business on a 6 Month fixed term contract based at Vista, part of the Eurocell Group of companies in Prenton.
This role focuses on providing a positive customer experience, while supporting production planning, order processing and operational efficiency.
WHAT OUR SALES ADMINISTRATORS DO:
- Collaborate effectively with sales, production, and operations teams to achieve business objectives
- Process customer and online orders accurately and efficiently
- Manage order administration, including amendments, scheduling, and capacity planning
- Resolve order queries, discrepancies, and outstanding issues promptly
- Maintain pricing, quotations, proformas, and production schedules to support operational efficiency
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer enquiries via phone and email
- Build strong customer relationships through a proactive, responsive, and solutions-focused approach

WHAT WE NEED FROM OUR SALES ADMINISTRATORS:
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy in data entry and order processing
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal
- Good IT skills, including experience with order processing systems and Microsoft Office
- Ability to understand and optimise cutting layouts for flat panels - training provided

WHAT WE OFFER OUR SALES ADMINISTRATORS:

title: Document Controller
description:
Reynco Ltd is working in partnership with a well-established Construction Contracting group, who is seeking a highly organised and detail-oriented Document Controller to join their expanding team. The Document Controller will provide administrative support to the Pre-Construction Team and ensure the smooth and efficient operation of all project-related activities.

Remuneration:

Salary: 30,000 - 40,000 Depending on Experience + Bonus, Pension & Additional Benefits
Location: The Wirral

Key Responsibilities:
- Maintain a document control system to manage all project documentation and ensure that all files are up-to-date and accurate.
- Issuing, tracking, and logging incoming/outgoing drawings, documents and correspondence.
- Edit documentation to ensure that all documents are consistent, accurate, and comply with company standards.
- Supporting project teams with the collation of O&M manuals and As-Built documentation.
- Assist in the preparation of project proposals, bids, and contracts.
- Collaborate with the project team to develop and maintain project plans, schedules, and budgets.
- Perform other administrative tasks as required.

Skills & Experience:
- Proven experience in a document control, project coordination, site administration or a similar role.
- Familiarity with document control platforms (4 Projects, Aconex, Asite, Viewpoint) would be desirable.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficiency in MS Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
- Attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Diversity & Inclusion

Reynco Ltd operate an inclusive and diverse recruitment process, whilst also ensuring our clients do the same and we can provide any advice or education to them in relation to this. If there may be any support or adjustments required at any point throughout your recruitment journey with us, then please let us know and our trained consultants will assist and advise you accordingly.
